title: Statistical tools in base R
source: Code from "Statistical Analysis using RStudio", UP Mindanao SPARCS on dev.to (April 2025)
intro: Watch RStudio describe the temperatures in R's built-in airquality data. For each line, the coach selects it in statistical-tools.R and presses Run. It explains the numbers after the Console prints them.

steps.title: Minimum and maximum: min() and max()

runs.code: sample_data <- airquality # Assigning the built-in dataset "airquality" to sample_data
max(sample_data$Temp) # Finding the maximum value in Temperature
min(sample_data$Temp) # Finding the minimum value in Temperature

steps.explain: `sample_data` is a copy of `airquality`: daily readings from New York, May to September 1973. `$Temp` picks the temperature column, which holds each day's highest temperature in °F. The hottest day reached {max} °F. The coolest day only reached {min} °F.

steps.title: Mean: mean()

runs.code: mean(sample_data$Temp) # Finding the mean/average of all Temperature entries

steps.explain: The mean adds up every daily temperature and divides by the number of days. Here it is {mean} °F. `Temp` has no missing values. If it had any, `mean()` would return `NA` unless you added `na.rm = TRUE`.

steps.title: Median: median()

runs.code: median(sample_data$Temp) # Finding the median of Temperature

steps.explain: If you sort the temperatures from coolest to hottest, the middle one is {median} °F. That is a little higher than the mean of {mean} °F. The coolest days pull the mean down, but they barely move the middle value.

steps.title: Percentiles: quantile()

runs.code: quantile(sample_data$Temp) # Return the percentiles of 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100
quantile(sample_data$Temp, c(0.45)) # Return only the 45th percentile

steps.explain: With no other arguments, `quantile()` gives the 0th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 100th percentiles. About a quarter of the days reached {p25} °F or less, and about three quarters reached {p75} °F or less. The 0% and 100% values are the minimum and maximum, and 50% is the median. `c(0.45)` asks for just one percentile: about 45% of the days reached {p45} °F or less.

steps.title: Summary: summary()

runs.code: summary(sample_data$Temp) # Return the summary of Temperature in airquality dataset

steps.explain: `summary()` shows six numbers at once: minimum {s_min}, first quartile {s_q1}, median {s_median}, mean {s_mean}, third quartile {s_q3} and maximum {s_max}. They are the same results as the earlier steps. `summary()` rounds to four significant figures, so the mean of {mean} appears as {s_mean}.
